polity.q: The 6th Schedule of the Constitution provides for:
o: Administration of Tribal Areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram
Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in general
polity.e: The 6th Schedule provides for autonomous District Councils and Regional Councils for tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram — giving tribal communities substantial self-governance powers.

polity.q: The Preamble uses the phrase 'We, the People of India'. Which of the following constitutional features is most directly derived from this phrase?
o: The federal structure of the Constitution
The provision for a bicameral legislature
polity.e: 'We, the People' establishes that the Constitution derives its authority from the citizens of India, embodying the principle of popular sovereignty.

polity.q: What is the minimum age for a person to become a member of a Panchayat?
polity.e: Article 243F prescribes the minimum age for Panchayat membership as 21 years.

polity.q: What is the minimum age for a person to become a member of Rajya Sabha?
polity.e: A person must be at least 30 years old to be elected to the Rajya Sabha.

polity.q: Which body conducts elections for Panchayati Raj institutions in Tamil Nadu?
polity.e: The Tamil Nadu State Election Commission is responsible for conducting local body elections.

polity.q: Which landmark case established the 'basic structure' doctrine, limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution, and affirmed judicial review as part of that basic structure?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
polity.e: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution, including judicial review.

polity.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Tamil Nadu Legislature to make laws on matters in the State List?
polity.e: Article 246 defines the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and States via the Seventh Schedule.

polity.q: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is available only to citizens and not to foreigners?
polity.e: Article 19 freedoms (speech, assembly, etc.) are available only to citizens.

polity.q: Which article enables the High Courts to issue writs?
polity.e: Article 226 empowers every High Court to issue writs including Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Certiorari, Prohibition, and Quo Warranto for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.

polity.q: What is the maximum period allowed for the dissolution of a municipality before fresh elections must be held?
polity.e: Article 243U allows a municipality a term of five years, but if dissolved earlier, elections must be held within six months.

polity.q: The Right to Freedom of Religion under Article 25 is subject to which set of limitations?
polity.e: Article 25 provides freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion, subject to public order, morality and health.

polity.q: The S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) case relates to:
o: Imposition of President's Rule under Art 356
polity.e: S.R. Bommai (1994) — 9-judge bench — held that President's Rule is subject to judicial review, the floor test must be the only way to determine majority, and secularism is part of Basic Structure.

polity.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added which schedule?
polity.e: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats, added by the 73rd Amendment.

polity.q: Which of the following cases falls under the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?
polity.e: Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in disputes between the Government of India and states or between states.

polity.q: During a national emergency, the enforcement of which fundamental rights can never be suspended by the President under Article 359?
polity.e: The 44th Amendment (1978) ensures that Articles 20 (protection in respect of conviction) and 21 (life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended even during emergency.

polity.q: Which body is responsible for the preparation of electoral rolls in India?
polity.e: The Election Commission of India prepares and updates electoral rolls for all constituencies.

polity.q: Who among the following appoints the Prime Minister of India?
polity.e: As per Article 75 of the Constitution, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President.

polity.q: The presiding officer of a Joint Sitting of Parliament is:
polity.e: Joint sittings (Art 108) are presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha, or in his absence, the Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha, or if he is also absent, the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

polity.q: The maximum number of members in a State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) cannot exceed:
o: One-third of the total members of the State Legislative Assembly
One-fourth of the total members of the State Assembly
polity.e: Article 171 states that the total number of members in a Vidhan Parishad shall not exceed one-third of the total members of the Vidhan Sabha, and shall not be less than 40 members.

polity.q: Under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution, which of the following writs is issued to a lower court or tribunal to transfer a case pending before it to a higher court or to quash its order?
polity.e: Certiorari is issued to quash the order of a lower court or tribunal; Prohibition is preventive, while Mandamus commands performance of duty.

polity.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act is related to:
polity.e: It added Part IX to the Constitution, providing a framework for Panchayati Raj institutions.

polity.q: Which article of the Constitution provides for the establishment of a State Election Commission for Panchayati Raj institutions?
polity.e: Article 243K mandates the creation of a State Election Commission for superintendence of Panchayat elections.

polity.q: Which of the following fundamental rights can be suspended during a national emergency?
polity.e: Article 19 can be suspended under Article 358, while Article 21 cannot be suspended as per the 44th Amendment.

polity.q: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is specifically available to minorities in India?
o: Right to establish and administer educational institutions (Article 30)
Right to move freely throughout India (Article 19)
polity.e: Article 30 grants linguistic and religious minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

polity.q: Which of the following committees of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru?
polity.e: Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee and the States Committee (for negotiating with princely states). The Drafting Committee was chaired by Ambedkar.

polity.q: The minimum age for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court of India is:
polity.e: The Constitution does not prescribe a minimum age for Supreme Court judges; only a retirement age of 65.

polity.q: Which Directive Principle was added by the 42nd Amendment to protect and improve the environment?
polity.e: Article 48A, added by the 42nd Amendment, directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.

polity.q: Which Amendment to the Indian Constitution inserted the words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' into the Preamble?
polity.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. It also amended many other parts of the Constitution.

polity.q: The Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission consists of a Chairperson and how many members?
polity.e: As per the Protection of Human Rights Act, a State Human Rights Commission has a Chairperson and two members.

polity.q: Which of the following parliamentary committees does NOT include members from the Rajya Sabha?
o: Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
polity.e: The Estimates Committee consists only of members from Lok Sabha; other major financial committees have representation from Rajya Sabha.

polity.q: Which of the following statements about the Prime Minister of India is correct?
o: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairperson of the NITI Aayog
The Prime Minister is elected directly by the people
The Prime Minister serves a fixed term of five years
The Prime Minister can be removed by the President without Parliament's approval
polity.e: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio chairperson of the NITI Aayog, as per its governing council structure.

polity.q: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the inclusion of:
polity.e: The Swaran Singh Committee recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution. Acting on this, the 42nd Amendment (1976) added Part IV-A with Article 51A containing 10 Fundamental Duties.

polity.q: Which of the following is a condition for the President to exercise the power of pardon under Article 72?
o: The pardon can be granted only after a conviction by a court-martial
The President must consult the Prime Minister before granting pardon
The power extends to cases where the sentence is a death sentence
The pardon can be granted only for offences against laws made by the State Legislature
polity.e: Article 72(1)(c) specifically includes cases where the sentence is of death, and the power extends to all offences against Union laws, court-martial, and death sentences.

polity.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the State Government in India as per the Constitution?
o: Council of Ministers headed by Chief Minister
polity.e: Only some states have a bicameral legislature; most have a unicameral system.

polity.q: The concept of 'Judicial Review' in India is borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
polity.e: Judicial Review, the power of courts to examine the constitutionality of laws, is inspired by the US Constitution.

polity.q: Under which Article is the practice of 'untouchability' abolished?
polity.e: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.

polity.q: The power to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill rests with the:
polity.e: Under Article 110, the Speaker of Lok Sabha certifies a Bill as a Money Bill, and his decision is final.

polity.q: Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which articles of the Indian Constitution?
polity.e: Part IV of the Constitution, covering Articles 36 to 51, lays down the Directive Principles of State Policy.

polity.q: Under which Article can the President remove a Governor from office?
polity.e: Article 156 states that the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President, implying removal by the President.

polity.q: What is the term of office of the President of India?
o: Five years from the date of election
Five years from the date of assuming office
Five years from the date of notification
Not fixed, depends on President's discretion
polity.e: Article 56 states that the President holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.

polity.q: Which of the following is a Gandhian principle enshrined in the Directive Principles?
polity.e: Article 40 directs the State to organize village panchayats, reflecting Gandhian philosophy.

polity.q: The 74th Amendment to the Constitution deals with which type of local bodies?
polity.e: The 74th Amendment (1992) added Part IX-A, covering Municipalities and urban local bodies.

polity.q: Who appoints the Chief Justice and other Judges of the High Court in a state?
polity.e: The President appoints the Chief Justice and other judges of a High Court after consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor.

polity.q: The judges of the Supreme Court of India are appointed by the ...
polity.e: The President appoints Supreme Court judges after consulting the Chief Justice of India.

polity.q: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the Right to Constitutional Remedies guaranteed?
polity.e: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights, making it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

polity.q: The right to constitutional remedies is considered the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution by which jurist?
polity.e: Dr B.R. Ambedkar called the Right to Constitutional Remedies the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

polity.q: The term 'Republic' in the Preamble of India signifies that:
o: The head of state is hereditary
The head of state is elected
The people have no voting rights
polity.e: 'Republic' means the head of state (President) is elected, not hereditary.

polity.q: Which constitutional amendment inserted Article 39A into the Directive Principles, providing for free legal aid?
polity.e: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added Article 39A to promote equal justice and free legal aid.

polity.q: In the context of DPSP, which Article directs the State to secure a uniform civil code for all citizens?
polity.e: Article 44 of the DPSP urges the state to endeavor for a uniform civil code.

polity.q: Which article empowers the Parliament to create new States or alter the boundaries of existing States?
polity.e: Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new States by separation, union, or merger of existing States, or by altering boundaries, names, or areas.

polity.q: In Tamil Nadu's three-tier Panchayati Raj system, the intermediate level is called?
polity.e: Tamil Nadu has Village Panchayat (lower), Panchayat Union (intermediate), and District Panchayat (upper).

polity.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the President?
polity.e: Article 54 provides for the election of the President by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and state legislatures.

polity.q: The term of office of a Member of Rajya Sabha is?
polity.e: Rajya Sabha members serve a term of six years, with one-third retiring every two years.

polity.q: Under which Article is the Right to Freedom of Religion guaranteed?
polity.e: Article 25 provides freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

polity.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution establishes the Supreme Court?
polity.e: Article 124 provides for the establishment of the Supreme Court of India. Other articles deal with related matters like acting Chief Justice or additional judges.

polity.q: What is the term of office for a member of a Panchayat in Tamil Nadu?
polity.e: As per the Tamil Nadu Panchayats Act, the term of a Panchayat member is five years.

polity.q: The concept of 'one person, one vote' is enshrined in which article of the Constitution?
polity.e: Article 326 provides for adult suffrage (universal adult franchise) ensuring each person has one vote.

polity.q: The District Planning Committee (DPC) is constituted under which article?
polity.e: Article 243ZD provides for the constitution of District Planning Committees to consolidate plans for the district.

polity.q: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) is called:
polity.e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is called the 'Mini Constitution' because of the sweeping changes it made.

polity.q: Which of the following is NOT a qualification required for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court of India?
o: Must be a citizen of India.
Must have been a judge of a High Court for at least five years.
Must have been an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years.
Must have served as a District Judge for at least five years.
polity.e: Service as a District Judge is a qualification for High Court judges, not directly for Supreme Court judges.

history.q: The practice of sati was banned in India in which year?
history.e: The practice of sati was banned in 1829 by Lord William Bentinck.

history.q: The Vedic Age refers to the period of composition of the Vedas. Which Veda is the oldest?
history.e: The Rig Veda, composed around 1500-1200 BCE, is the oldest of the four Vedas.

history.q: Which Maratha battle in 1761 saw a decisive defeat against Ahmad Shah Abdali?
history.e: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was a major defeat for the Marathas against the Afghan invader Ahmad Shah Abdali.

history.q: The ancient Roman settlement found in Tamil Nadu is:
history.e: Arikamedu (near Puducherry) was an ancient Roman trading settlement (1st century BCE - 2nd century CE) where Roman pottery, amphorae, and glass were found.

history.q: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in:
history.e: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement on 1 August 1920 (following the Khilafat grievances and Jallianwala Bagh massacre). Indians were asked to boycott British courts, schools, goods, and legislature. Suspended after Chauri Chaura violence (February 1922).

history.q: The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of which ruler?
history.e: Hiuen Tsang toured India in the 7th century AD, mostly under the patronage of Harshavardhana.

history.q: The Vijayanagara ruler who patronized the Telugu poet Allasani Peddana was:
history.e: Krishnadevaraya was a great patron of literature; Allasani Peddana was the 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha' in his court.

history.q: Operation Polo (1948) was related to:
history.e: Operation Polo (September 1948): Indian military action (police action) to integrate the princely state of Hyderabad into India after Nizam Osman Ali Khan refused to accede.

history.q: The 'Kudi Arasu' journal was started by:
history.e: 'Kudi Arasu' (Republic) was a Tamil journal started by Periyar E.V. Ramasamy in 1925 to propagate self-respect ideology and rational thinking.

history.q: Under which Maratha ruler did the Peshwa post become hereditary?
history.e: After Shivaji's death, the Peshwa post became hereditary under Shahuji (Shahu), with Balaji Vishwanath as first Peshwa.

history.q: The epic 'Mahabharata' was originally composed by:
history.e: The Mahabharata was composed by Vyasa (also called Krishna Dvaipayana or Veda Vyasa). The original was called 'Jaya' (8,800 verses), expanded to 'Bharata' (24,000), then 'Mahabharata' (100,000 verses).

history.q: The Buddhist Tripitaka (Three Baskets) were originally composed in which language?
history.e: The Tripitaka were originally composed and preserved in Pali, the language of the Theravada Buddhist canon.

history.q: The 'Dancing Girl' bronze figurine belongs to which site?
history.e: The bronze dancing girl found at Mohenjo-daro showcases the metallurgical and artistic skills of the Harappans.

history.q: The Fourth Buddhist Council, which resulted in the compilation of the Abhidhamma Pitaka, was held during the reign of which ruler?
history.e: The Fourth Buddhist Council was convened under the patronage of Kushana ruler Kanishka in Kashmir.

history.q: The Buddha delivered his first sermon at Sarnath. This event is known as:
history.e: The first sermon, the Dhammachakkappavattana Sutta (Setting in Motion the Wheel of Dharma), was given at Sarnath to the five ascetics.

history.q: Which Maratha ruler was pensioned off after the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-1818)?
history.e: Baji Rao II, the last Peshwa, was defeated and pensioned, ending the Maratha Empire.

history.q: The Palaeolithic site 'Attirampakkam' is located near which city?
history.e: Attirampakkam is a Palaeolithic archaeological site near Chennai (formerly Madras), Tamil Nadu. Recent studies show stone tools here date back ~1.5 million years — among the oldest in India.

history.q: The anti-Hindi agitation in Tamil Nadu reached its peak in which year, leading to widespread protests and violence?
history.e: In 1965, massive protests erupted against the imposition of Hindi as the sole official language, leading to a policy of continued English usage.

history.q: The Indus Valley Civilization's writing system remains
history.e: The Indus Valley Civilization's writing system remains undeciphered.

history.q: Who became the first Indian to be the Governor-General of a dominion?
history.e: C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji) became the first (and only) Indian Governor-General of India (1948-1950), taking over from Lord Mountbatten. Earlier was the last Governor-General of British India.

history.q: Who was the Mughal emperor who granted the British East India Company the right to trade in India?
history.e: Jahangir granted the British East India Company the right to trade in India in 1612.

history.q: The Subsidiary Alliance system was introduced by:
history.e: Lord Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance system (1798) to bring Indian states under British control without direct annexation. Under this, Indian rulers had to maintain British troops at their cost.

history.q: The Kalinga State (modern Odisha) is associated with which ancient text?
history.e: The Hathigumpha (Elephant Cave) inscription at Udayagiri, Odisha records the deeds of King Kharavela of Kalinga (1st century BCE), the greatest ruler of ancient Kalinga.

history.q: The British East India Company established its first factory in India at which place in 1612?
history.e: The British East India Company established its first factory at Surat in 1612.

history.q: The British East India Company's monopoly over Indian trade was ended by the
history.e: The British East India Company's monopoly over Indian trade was ended by the Charter Act of 1813. This act opened up Indian trade to other British companies.

history.q: In which year was the Battle of Talikota fought?
history.e: The Battle of Talikota was fought in 1565.

history.q: In Jainism, the 'Angas' refer to:
history.e: The 12 Angas form the core of Jain canonical literature, originally compiled at the Vallabhi council.

history.q: The Nataraja (dancing Shiva) bronze sculpture was perfected during:
history.e: The iconic Nataraja bronze sculpture reached its artistic peak during the Chola period (9th-13th century CE). These images became the universal symbol of cosmic dance.

history.q: The Maratha kingdom under Shivaji Maharaj was formally established with the coronation at which fort in 1674?
history.e: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad Fort in 1674, marking the formal foundation of the Maratha Empire.

history.q: The Amara-Nayaka system in the Vijayanagara Empire was essentially a system of:
o: Military and land grants to Nayakas
history.e: The Amara-Nayaka system was a military-administrative system where Nayakas held land grants and provided troops to the king.

history.q: Theravada Buddhism is also called:
history.e: Theravada (Way of the Elders) Buddhism is also called Hinayana (Lesser Vehicle) by Mahayana Buddhists. It emphasizes personal salvation and the original Pali Canon.

history.q: The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was implemented by:
history.e: Lord Dalhousie implemented the Doctrine of Lapse to annex states without a natural heir.

history.q: Which is considered the earliest known Pandya inscription, dating to around 2nd-1st century BCE?
history.e: The Mangulam inscription, found near Madurai, records a donation by a Pandya king and is the earliest Pandya epigraph.

history.q: Who among the following was a prominent social reformer from Tamil Nadu?
history.e: E.V. Ramasamy, also known as Periyar, was a prominent social reformer from Tamil Nadu. He advocated for social justice and equality.

history.q: The practice of Sati was abolished by which of the following British officials in India?
history.e: Lord William Bentinck, as Governor-General, abolished Sati through the Bengal Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII).

history.q: The Theosophical Society was founded in 1875 by which two individuals?
o: Helena Blavatsky and Henry Steel Olcott
Annie Besant and Charles Webster Leadbeater
history.e: Helena Blavatsky and Henry Steel Olcott founded the Theosophical Society.

history.q: The Mauryan Empire, which ruled much of India after the Vedic period, was founded by which ruler?
history.e: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire.

history.q: 'Vetti' in Chola inscriptions refers to:
history.e: Vetti (also veth/begari) was forced labor extracted by the state in Chola period, distinct from regular taxation. Villagers had to render free service to the king.

history.q: The Indus Valley Civilization's trade links with Mesopotamia are evidenced by the discovery of which of the following?
history.e: Harappan seals found in Mesopotamian cities like Ur confirm long-distance trade between the two civilizations.

history.q: Rishabhanatha, the first Tirthankara of Jainism, is also known by which name?
history.e: Rishabhanatha is also called Adinatha, meaning 'first lord', and is considered the founder of Jainism in the present cosmic cycle.

history.q: The 'Goa Liberation' from Portuguese rule took place in which year?
history.e: Indian armed forces liberated Goa from Portuguese colonial rule on December 19, 1961, through Operation Vijay.

history.q: Which personality was associated with the Theosophical Society and the Home Rule Movement in India?
history.e: Annie Besant revived the Theosophical Society in India and launched the Home Rule Movement in 1916.

history.q: Which Greek ambassador visited the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
history.e: Megasthenes, a Greek envoy from Seleucus Nicator, visited Chandragupta Maurya's court and wrote 'Indica'.

history.q: The Viceroy during the Quit India Movement was:
history.e: Lord Linlithgow was Viceroy (1936-1943) during the Quit India Movement (August 1942). He immediately arrested all Congress leaders and suppressed the movement harshly.

history.q: Which Ashokan edict mentions the Cholas, Pandyas, Satyaputras, and Keralaputras?
history.e: Major Rock Edict II records the southern kingdoms as part of Ashoka's Dhamma outreach.

history.q: The 'Land of the Seven Pagodas' is a historical reference to the port city of which ancient Tamil kingdom?
history.e: Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram), the Pallava port, was called the 'Land of the Seven Pagodas' by European sailors.

history.q: Which of the following pairs of British Acts and their provisions is correctly matched?
o: Regulating Act, 1773 - Established the Supreme Court at Calcutta
Pitt's India Act, 1784 - Abolished the Board of Control
Charter Act, 1833 - Ended the monopoly of the East India Company in tea trade
Government of India Act, 1858 - Introduced Dyarchy in provinces
history.e: The Regulating Act of 1773 established the Supreme Court at Calcutta, while Pitt's India Act created the Board of Control.

history.q: The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded by which of the following brothers?
history.e: The Vijayanagara kingdom was founded by Harihara and Bukka, two brothers who were local chieftains.

history.q: Which Chola ruler is credited with the systematic introduction of the 'Valanadu' administrative division?
history.e: Rajaraja I reorganized the Chola empire into mandalams, valanadus, and nadus, with valanadus being districts under royal officers.

history.q: The post-Gupta period saw the rise of the Vardhana dynasty. Which of the following statements about Harshavardhana is incorrect?
o: He was a patron of Nalanda University
His court poet Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita
He defeated the Chalukya king Pulakesin II
history.e: Harsha was defeated by Pulakesin II on the banks of Narmada, not the other way.

history.q: Which British governor-general introduced the Permanent Settlement?
history.e: Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement. It was a system of land revenue collection.

history.q: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of which Gupta ruler?
history.e: Fa-Hien traveled to India in the early 5th century AD, primarily during the reign of Chandragupta II.

history.q: Which of the following Pallava monuments is a 'rath' (chariot) carved from a single rock, part of the 'Pancha Rathas' complex at Mamallapuram?
history.e: The Pancha Rathas include Draupadi Ratha, the smallest monolithic rath. Arjuna's Penance is a bas-relief; Shore Temple is structural.

history.q: The Great Bath, a large public bathing structure, was found at which Indus Valley site?
history.e: The Great Bath is a notable structure at Mohenjo-daro, used for ritual bathing.

history.q: The 'Lion Capital' of Ashoka, now the national emblem of India, belongs to which period?
history.e: The Lion Capital is a Mauryan sculpture from the 3rd century BCE, erected by Emperor Ashoka at Sarnath.

history.q: The Indian Rebellion of 1857 started in which city?
history.e: The Indian Rebellion of 1857 started in Meerut.

history.q: Lord Hastings was Governor-General during the:
history.e: Lord Hastings (Francis Rawdon-Hastings, Governor-General 1813-1823) fought the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-1818), which ended the Peshwa's power.

history.q: The Pallava dynasty was overthrown by
history.e: The Pallava dynasty was overthrown by the Chola dynasty in the 9th century.

history.q: Which of the following rivers is associated with the Indus Valley Civilization?
history.e: The Indus Valley Civilization is associated with the Indus river. It was a major river of the civilization.

geography.q: Hirakud Dam (world's longest earthen dam) is on:
geography.e: Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi river in Odisha is one of the world's longest earthen dams at 25.8 km. It forms Hirakud reservoir, one of India's largest artificial lakes.

geography.q: The Pulicat Lake (Pulicat Bird Sanctuary) is located on the border of:
geography.e: Pulicat Lake (Pulicat or Pazhaverkadu) is the second largest brackish water lagoon in India, located on the Tamil Nadu-Andhra Pradesh border. It is famous for flamingos and migratory birds. The greater part is in Andhra Pradesh.

geography.q: The highest peak in the Western Ghats is:
geography.e: Anamudi (2,695 m) in the Anamalai Hills of Kerala is the highest peak in the Western Ghats and also the highest peak in South India outside the Himalayas.

geography.q: Which of the following soil types is commonly found in the delta regions of Tamil Nadu?
geography.e: Alluvial soil is commonly found in the delta regions of Tamil Nadu and is suitable for growing crops such as rice and sugarcane.

geography.q: In which year was the Mullaperiyar dam on the Periyar river constructed?
geography.e: The Mullaperiyar dam was constructed in 1895.

geography.q: India's first Metro rail was established in:
geography.e: Kolkata Metro was India's first metro rail system, inaugurated on 24 October 1984 (though partial opening was in 1983). Delhi Metro (2002) is currently the largest metro network in India.

geography.q: The National Animal of India is:
geography.e: The Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris tigris) is India's national animal (since 1973, replacing the lion). India has ~70% of the world's tiger population. Project Tiger (1973) helped increase numbers from 1,827 (1973) to 3,167+ (2022 census).

geography.q: Which state in India has the largest area of black soils?
geography.e: Maharashtra has the largest area of black soils, which are found in the Vidarbha and Marathwada regions.

geography.q: What type of soil is characterized by high iron and aluminum content?
geography.e: Laterite soil has high iron and aluminum content.

geography.q: What is the name of the soil type that is predominantly found in the Tamil Nadu region?
geography.e: Red soil is the predominant soil type found in Tamil Nadu.

geography.q: What is the primary source of rainfall in Tamil Nadu?
geography.e: The Northeast Monsoon is the primary source of rainfall in Tamil Nadu, bringing significant rainfall to the state from October to December.

geography.q: The 'Mahanadi' river originates from which state?
geography.e: The Mahanadi originates from the Sihawa range in Chhattisgarh and flows into Odisha.

geography.q: The McMahon Line is the boundary between:
geography.e: The McMahon Line (1914, Simla Convention) is the disputed boundary between India and China (Tibet) in the northeastern Himalayas. China does not recognize this line; it claims Arunachal Pradesh as 'South Tibet'.

geography.q: OPEC (Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries) was founded in:
geography.e: OPEC was founded in 1960 in Baghdad by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela. Today it has 13 members. OPEC controls ~40% of world oil production. Its secretariat is in Vienna, Austria.

geography.q: Which of the following ports is located in Tamil Nadu?
geography.e: The Chennai port is located in Tamil Nadu.

geography.q: What is the name of the process by which water moves through a plant, from the roots to the atmosphere?
geography.e: Transpiration is the process by which water moves through a plant.

geography.q: What is the name of the river that flows through the city of Madurai in Tamil Nadu?
geography.e: The Vaigai river is a major river in Tamil Nadu and flows through the city of Madurai. It is approximately 258 km long and is an important source of water for irrigation.

geography.q: The Nathula Pass connects:
geography.e: Nathula Pass (4,310 m) connects Sikkim (India) with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. It was reopened in 2006 for limited bilateral trade after being closed since the 1962 Sino-Indian War.

geography.q: What type of soil is formed through the weathering of granite and gneiss rocks?
geography.e: Red soils are formed through the weathering of granite and gneiss rocks.

geography.q: What is the name of the hill station located in the Dindigul district?
geography.e: Kodaikanal is a popular hill station located in the Dindigul district.

geography.q: In which region of India are the majority of alluvial soils found?
geography.e: The northern plains of India have the largest area of alluvial soils, formed by river deposits.

geography.q: Which river flows through the cities of Tiruchirappalli and Thanjavur?
geography.e: The Cauvery river flows through the cities of Tiruchirappalli and Thanjavur.

geography.q: Which mountain range runs along the western coast of India and influences the climate of the region?
geography.e: The Western Ghats mountain range runs along the western coast of India and influences the climate of the region.

geography.q: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) headquarters is in:
geography.e: NATO's political headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium (moved from Paris in 1967). Its military headquarters (Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe — SHAPE) is in Mons, Belgium.

geography.q: Which of the following types of natural resources is abundant in the Gulf of Mannar?
geography.e: The Gulf of Mannar is known for its rich fisheries resources. It supports a significant fishing industry.

geography.q: India's Silicon Valley is:
geography.e: Bengaluru (Bangalore) is called India's Silicon Valley due to concentration of IT companies — Infosys, Wipro, HAL, ISRO are headquartered here. It is also called the 'Pub Capital', 'Garden City', 'Startup Capital of India'.

geography.q: What is the primary crop grown in the Kaveri Delta region?
geography.e: Rice is the primary crop grown in the Kaveri Delta region.

geography.q: What is the capital of Tamil Nadu's Nilgiri district?
geography.e: Ooty (Udhagamandalam) is the district headquarters of the Nilgiri district in Tamil Nadu, and a popular hill station.

geography.q: What is the name of the dam built across the Bhavani River?
geography.e: The Bhavanisagar Dam is a major dam built across the Bhavani River in Tamil Nadu. It is used for irrigation and hydroelectric power generation.

geography.q: The Western Ghats are a biodiversity hotspot. How many biodiversity hotspots are there globally?
geography.e: There are 36 global biodiversity hotspots as recognized by Conservation International. India has 4 hotspots: Western Ghats, Eastern Himalayas, Indo-Burma region, and Sundaland (includes Andaman & Nicobar).

geography.q: India is situated on which tectonic plate?
geography.e: India sits on the Indo-Australian Plate. The collision of this plate with the Eurasian Plate formed the Himalayas.

geography.q: The 'Loo' is a hot dry wind blowing over:
geography.e: The Loo is a hot, dry, dust-laden wind that blows over the North Indian plains (Rajasthan, UP, Bihar, Punjab, Haryana) during May-June. Temperatures can reach 45-48°C during Loo conditions.

geography.q: Which of the following districts in Tamil Nadu has the highest population density?
geography.e: Chennai district has the highest population density in Tamil Nadu (Census 2011).

geography.q: The Siachen glacier is in:
geography.e: The Siachen glacier lies in the eastern Karakoram Range.

geography.q: What is the name of the railway zone that covers Tamil Nadu?
geography.e: The Southern Railway zone covers the state of Tamil Nadu.

geography.q: India's first nuclear power plant was at:
geography.e: India's first nuclear power plant, the Tarapur Atomic Power Station in Maharashtra, began operating in 1969.

geography.q: The Mettur Dam is built across which river?
geography.e: Mettur Dam (Stanley Reservoir) is built across the river Kaveri in Salem district, Tamil Nadu. Constructed in 1934, it is one of the largest dams in India. Water is released for Kuruvai cultivation in the delta.

geography.q: Which soil is most suitable for cotton cultivation in India?
geography.e: Black soil (Regur soil) is most suitable for cotton cultivation as it has good moisture retention. The Deccan Plateau is famous for this type of soil.

geography.q: Which of the following regions in the world experiences a climate similar to the Mediterranean climate?
geography.e: Central Chile has a Mediterranean-type climate with dry summers and mild, wet winters, resembling the Mediterranean basin.

geography.q: In which state of India can the laterite soil type be predominantly found?
geography.e: Laterite soil is predominantly found in Kerala.

geography.q: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous ranges that run along which coast?
geography.e: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous ranges running along the eastern coast (Coromandel Coast) of India, from Odisha to Tamil Nadu.

geography.q: Which river is the longest in Tamil Nadu?
geography.e: The Cauvery (about 800 km in total) is the longest river flowing through Tamil Nadu.

economics.q: Which economic concept refers to the increase in the overall price level of goods and services in an economy?
economics.e: Inflation refers to the increase in the overall price level of goods and services in an economy, reducing the purchasing power of money.

economics.q: What is the name of the international trade agreement signed by India in 1995 to promote global trade and economic cooperation?
economics.e: The WTO Agreement was signed by India in 1995 to promote global trade and economic cooperation.

economics.q: The Contingency Fund of India is kept at the disposal of:
economics.e: The Contingency Fund of India (Article 267) is at the President's disposal for urgent unforeseen expenditures. Its size is Rs 500 crore; Parliament must ratify later.

economics.q: Which organization replaced the Planning Commission of India in 2015?
economics.e: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015 to foster cooperative federalism.

economics.q: What is the name of the national agency responsible for monitoring and regulating foreign trade in India?
economics.e: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade is the national agency responsible for monitoring and regulating foreign trade in India.

economics.q: The Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) Index was published by the World Bank under which report?
economics.e: World Bank's 'Doing Business Report' published EoDB rankings from 2003 to 2021 (discontinued). India improved from rank 142 (2014) to 63 (2019). Report discontinued after data integrity concerns.

economics.q: What is the term for the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders over a given time period?
economics.e: Gross Domestic Product is the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders. It is a key indicator of economic growth.

economics.q: What is the name of the commission that recommends the minimum support price for crops in India?
o: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
economics.e: The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices recommends the minimum support price for crops.

economics.q: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) consists of how many members, and who has the casting vote?
economics.e: MPC: 6 members — 3 from RBI (Governor, 2 Deputy Governors) + 3 external members appointed by Government. RBI Governor chairs and has casting vote in case of tie. Meets every 2 months. Inflation target: 4% ± 2%.

economics.q: In which year did the Government of India introduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
economics.e: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in 2017 to simplify the tax structure in India.

economics.q: Which of the following is NOT a component of national income as per the expenditure method?
economics.e: Transfer payments are not included as they are not payments for current production.

economics.q: What is the budgeting approach that involves allocating resources based on performance and outcomes?
economics.e: Performance-Based Budgeting involves allocating resources based on performance and outcomes. It helps to improve efficiency and effectiveness in public spending.

economics.q: What is the term for the value of goods and services produced by a country's citizens, regardless of location?
economics.e: GNP measures the value of goods and services produced by a country's citizens.

economics.q: Which scheme was launched by the government to provide employment guarantee to rural laborers?
economics.e: The MGNREGA scheme was launched by the government to provide employment guarantee to rural laborers, ensuring a minimum of 100 days of wage employment per year.

economics.q: What is the role of the Finance Commission in the context of Indian federalism?
o: To allocate funds for the Five-Year Plans
To determine the sharing of taxes between the center and states
To oversee the implementation of budgetary policies
economics.e: The Finance Commission decides the tax-sharing formula between the center and states.

economics.q: What is the name of the economic planning body that was established in 1950 to promote India's economic development?
economics.e: Planning Commission was established in 1950.

economics.q: What is the term for trade between countries without restrictions or tariffs?
economics.e: Free trade refers to international trade without restrictions, tariffs, or quotas. It aims to promote economic cooperation and growth among nations.

economics.q: What is the name of the scheme launched by the Government of India to provide financial support to farmers?
economics.e: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi provides financial support.

economics.q: Which of the following schemes is launched by the Government of India to promote financial inclusion?
economics.e: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana promotes financial inclusion. It aims to provide banking services to the unbanked population.

economics.q: What is the budgeting approach that focuses on the outcomes and results of government expenditures?
economics.e: Outcome Budgeting focuses on the outcomes and results of government expenditures, aiming to achieve specific goals and objectives.

economics.q: Which of the following correctly represents the relationship between National Income (NI), Net National Product at Market Price (NNP_MP), and Net Indirect Taxes (NIT)?
economics.e: National Income (NI) is NNP at factor cost, which equals NNP at market price minus net indirect taxes.

economics.q: Masala Bonds are rupee-denominated bonds issued by Indian entities in:
o: Only in the London Stock Exchange
economics.e: Masala Bonds: rupee-denominated bonds issued by Indian entities (corporates, government-backed) in overseas markets. Currency risk borne by foreign investors. First issued by IFC (World Bank arm) in 2014 on LSE.

economics.q: Quantitative Easing (QE) involves a central bank:
o: Raising interest rates to curb inflation
Buying financial assets to inject liquidity
Selling government securities to absorb liquidity
economics.e: QE: central bank purchases government bonds/other assets from commercial banks to inject money into the economy, lower long-term rates, and stimulate growth when rates near zero.

economics.q: Under the NITI Aayog's 'Multidimensional Poverty Index' (MPI), which of the following dimensions is NOT directly considered?
economics.e: MPI measures deprivations in health, education, and standard of living using 12 indicators; income per capita is not a direct dimension.

economics.q: UNCTAD (United Nations Conference on Trade and Development) is headquartered in:
economics.e: UNCTAD: established 1964; headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland (same as WTO). Publishes World Investment Report (FDI data), Trade and Development Report. India is a founding member.

economics.q: Which of the following organizations is responsible for regulating the insurance sector in India?
economics.e: IRDA is the regulatory body for the insurance sector. It oversees the insurance industry in India.

economics.q: The Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC) is a joint initiative with which country?
economics.e: The Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor is being developed with Japanese financial and technical support.

economics.q: Which of the following taxes is a direct tax in India?
economics.e: Income tax is a direct tax, levied on individuals and businesses.

economics.q: What is the term for the difference between the revenue receipts and revenue expenditure in a budget?
economics.e: Revenue deficit is the difference between revenue receipts and revenue expenditure.

economics.q: Which of the following international trade agreements is signed by India to promote trade with Southeast Asian countries?
o: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation
economics.e: The ASEAN-India Free Trade Agreement is signed by India to promote trade with Southeast Asian countries. It reduces tariffs and promotes international trade.

economics.q: The Bombay Plan (1944) was drafted by Indian industrialists including Tata and Birla, proposing:
o: Free market economy with no government intervention
Central planning with significant state investment in industry
economics.e: Bombay Plan: 8 industrialists (JRD Tata, GD Birla, etc.) proposed a 15-year plan with heavy state investment in infrastructure and industry, import substitution, and mixed economy framework.

economics.q: India's forex reserves are managed by:
economics.e: The Reserve Bank of India manages India's foreign exchange reserves (foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the IMF reserve tranche) under the RBI Act and FEMA, 1999.

economics.q: The Heckscher-Ohlin theorem states that a country will export goods that are intensive in its:
economics.e: The H-O theorem: a country exports goods that intensively use its abundant factors. E.g., labour-abundant India exports labour-intensive goods.

economics.q: NABARD stands for:
o: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
National Banking Authority for Regional Development
National Association for Banking and Rural Districts
economics.e: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) was established in 1982. It provides credit for agricultural and rural development and supervises cooperative banks and RRBs.

economics.q: What is the name of the economic model adopted by India for its Five-Year Plans?
economics.e: India adopted a mixed economy model.

science.q: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
science.e: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis (translation). They read mRNA sequences and assemble amino acids into proteins.

science.q: Which scientist discovered the structure of DNA (Double Helix)?
o: Watson and Crick (with Franklin's X-ray data)
science.e: James Watson and Francis Crick discovered the double helix structure of DNA in 1953, using X-ray crystallography data from Rosalind Franklin. They received the Nobel Prize in 1962.

science.q: The pH of human blood is approximately:
science.e: Human blood pH is tightly regulated between 7.35-7.45 (slightly alkaline). Acidosis (pH < 7.35) and alkalosis (pH > 7.45) are life-threatening conditions. The body uses buffers (bicarbonate, phosphate) to maintain blood pH.

science.q: What is the main difference between a prokaryotic cell and a eukaryotic cell?
science.e: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus, while eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane.

science.q: The 'Montreal Protocol' is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of which substances?
science.e: The Montreal Protocol specifically targets the elimination of ozone-depleting substances like CFCs and halons.

science.q: A ball is dropped from a height of 80 m. How long does it take to reach the ground? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
Which polymer is used to make non-stick cookware?
science.e: Teflon (PTFE — polytetrafluoroethylene) is used for non-stick coatings. Its C-F bonds are very strong, making it chemically inert, heat-resistant, and giving it extremely low friction (non-stick property).

science.q: A body of mass 2 kg moving with a velocity of 10 m/s is brought to rest in 2 seconds by a constant force. The magnitude of the force is:
science.e: Acceleration = (0 - 10) / 2 = -5 m/s², so force = mass × acceleration = 2 × 5 = 10 N.

science.q: The 'kitchen of the cell' (food factory) is:
science.e: Chloroplasts are called the 'kitchen of the cell' because they carry out photosynthesis — using sunlight, CO₂, and water to produce glucose (food) and oxygen. Found only in plant cells. Contain chlorophyll.

science.q: Homi J. Bhabha is known as:
science.e: Dr. Homi J. Bhabha (1909-1966) is the Father of India's Nuclear Programme. He founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and Atomic Energy Establishment (now BARC). First Chairman of India's Atomic Energy Commission.

science.q: The primary site of photosynthesis in plants is the
science.e: Leaves contain abundant chloroplasts in mesophyll tissues where photosynthesis mainly occurs.

science.q: What force keeps us on the ground?
science.e: Gravity (gravitational force) is the force of attraction between the Earth and all objects on it. It keeps us grounded.

science.q: The term 'Biochemical Oxygen Demand' (BOD) is a measure of which of the following in a water body?
science.e: BOD measures the amount of dissolved oxygen needed by aerobic microorganisms to decompose organic matter in water.

science.q: Which is the largest organ in the human body?
science.e: The skin is the largest organ of the human body. It protects the body, regulates temperature, and provides sensation.

science.q: In human digestion, the enzyme pepsin acts on which nutrient in the stomach?
science.e: Pepsin is a proteolytic enzyme that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides in the acidic environment of the stomach.

science.q: The 'Paris Agreement' aims to limit global temperature increase to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels. Which of the following mechanisms is central to achieving this goal?
science.e: NDCs are the core of the Paris Agreement, requiring each country to set and update emission reduction targets.

science.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a distributed operating system?
o: It runs on a single computer
It manages multiple computers as a single system
It is designed for real-time applications
science.e: A distributed OS manages a group of independent computers and makes them appear as a single system to users.

science.q: Which of the following statements about lysosomes is correct?
o: They contain hydrolytic enzymes for digestion
science.e: Lysosomes are membrane-bound vesicles containing digestive enzymes that break down waste materials and foreign substances.

science.q: A person who cannot see distant objects clearly (near-sighted) has:
science.e: Myopia (short-sightedness): eyeball is too long or lens too curved; distant objects focus in front of retina. Corrected with concave (diverging/negative power) lens. Hypermetropia (long-sightedness): near objects focus behind retina; corrected with convex lens.

science.q: Which international agreement aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions?
science.e: The Kyoto Protocol is an international treaty that commits developed countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

science.q: In the reaction, 2FeCl3 + SnCl2 → 2FeCl2 + SnCl4, which pair acts as the oxidizing agent and reducing agent respectively?
science.e: FeCl3 is reduced (Fe3+ to Fe2+) – oxidizing agent; SnCl2 is oxidized (Sn2+ to Sn4+) – reducing agent.

science.q: The first artificial satellite was:
science.e: Sputnik 1 (Soviet Union, 4 October 1957) was the world's first artificial satellite. This launched the Space Age and the Space Race between USA and USSR. India's first satellite: Aryabhata (1975).

science.q: Polymers are large molecules made from:
science.e: Polymers are large molecules (macromolecules) made by linking many small repeating units called monomers. Natural polymers: rubber, cellulose, starch, proteins, DNA. Synthetic polymers: plastics (polyethylene, nylon, PVC).

science.q: BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) is a measure of:
science.e: BOD indicates the amount of oxygen required by microorganisms to decompose organic matter in water.

science.q: The process of converting excess glucose into glycogen for storage in the liver and muscles is called:
science.e: Glycogenesis: insulin stimulates the conversion of excess glucose to glycogen, stored in liver (up to 100g) and muscles (up to 400g). Glycogenolysis: glucagon/adrenaline stimulate glycogen breakdown to glucose when blood glucose falls.

science.q: Which of the following is an example of a combination reaction?
science.e: A combination reaction involves two or more reactants combining to form a single product.

science.q: Which substance is used as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils?
science.e: Nickel is commonly used as a catalyst in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils to produce margarine.

science.q: Superconductors are materials that:
o: Have zero electrical resistance below a critical temperature
Conduct electricity only in one direction
science.e: Superconductors exhibit zero electrical resistance below their critical temperature (Tc). Discovered by Heike Kamerlingh Onnes (1911) in mercury at 4.2 K. Used in MRI magnets, particle accelerators, maglev trains.

science.q: pH less than 7 indicates:
science.e: pH scale: 0-7 = acidic (H⁺ > OH⁻), pH 7 = neutral (pure water), pH 7-14 = basic/alkaline (OH⁻ > H⁺). Strong acids have pH near 0; strong bases near 14. Lemon juice pH~2; blood pH~7.4.

science.q: Which of the following is a chemical change?
science.e: Rusting involves formation of a new substance (iron oxide), indicating a chemical change.

science.q: Which of the following is a primary greenhouse gas released from landfills due to the anaerobic decomposition of organic waste?
science.e: Methane is produced by anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in landfills and is a potent greenhouse gas.

science.q: The atomic number of an element is:
o: The number of protons in the nucleus
The total number of protons and neutrons
The number of electrons in the outermost shell
science.e: Atomic number (Z) = number of protons in the nucleus. It uniquely identifies an element. For a neutral atom, atomic number = number of electrons. Mass number = protons + neutrons.

science.q: Which of the following is a type of malware that replicates itself and spreads to other computers?
science.e: A virus is a self-replicating program that spreads by attaching to files or programs.

science.q: Which of the following is the primary greenhouse gas emitted from paddy fields in Tamil Nadu due to anaerobic decomposition of organic matter?
science.e: Anaerobic decomposition in flooded paddy fields produces methane (CH4) by methanogenic archaea, a potent greenhouse gas.

science.q: Bernoulli's Principle states that:
o: In a fluid, increased velocity causes decreased pressure
Buoyancy equals weight of displaced fluid
science.e: Bernoulli's Principle: In a streamlined fluid flow, as velocity increases, pressure decreases. This explains lift in airplane wings, the Venturi effect, and why shower curtains are pulled inward.

science.q: Which type of muscle is involuntary and found in the walls of internal organs like the stomach and intestines?
science.e: Smooth muscle lacks striations and is controlled by the autonomic nervous system for peristalsis.

science.q: What is the function of an operating system?
science.e: Operating system manages all hardware and software resources, providing a user interface.

science.q: Which gas is most abundant in Earth's atmosphere?
science.e: Nitrogen (N2) makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere, followed by oxygen (21%), and argon (0.9%).

science.q: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
science.e: The pulmonary artery transports deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs for oxygenation.

science.q: Which of the following is an example of a decomposition reaction?
science.e: Electrolysis of water breaks down water into hydrogen and oxygen gases, which is a decomposition reaction.

science.q: Which of the following is a non-biodegradable waste?
science.e: Plastic bottles are synthetic polymers that do not decompose naturally, unlike organic materials.

science.q: Which type of reaction is represented by the equation: AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO₃?
science.e: This is a double displacement reaction where ions exchange between two compounds to form new compounds.

science.q: The main site of absorption of nutrients is:
science.e: The small intestine (particularly the jejunum) is the main site of nutrient absorption. Villi and microvilli (brush border) greatly increase surface area. Large intestine absorbs water and forms feces.

science.q: The term 'Biodiversity Hotspot' was coined by:
science.e: Norman Myers introduced the concept of biodiversity hotspots in 1988 to identify priority conservation areas.

science.q: The ozone layer is located in which atmospheric layer?
science.e: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere, approximately 15–35 km above Earth’s surface, absorbing harmful UV radiation.

science.q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy derived from organic matter, such as plant and animal waste?
science.e: Biomass energy is obtained from organic materials like wood, agricultural residues, and animal dung, and is renewable.

science.q: The nearest star to Earth (after the Sun) is:
science.e: Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth at 4.24 light years (about 40 trillion km). It is part of the Alpha Centauri triple star system. It has at least one exoplanet (Proxima b) in the habitable zone.

science.q: Nuclear fission is the process of:
o: Splitting a heavy nucleus into smaller fragments, releasing energy
Combining light nuclei to form heavier ones
science.e: Nuclear fission: a heavy nucleus (e.g., U-235) splits into smaller fragments when bombarded with neutrons, releasing enormous energy and more neutrons (chain reaction). Basis for nuclear power plants and atomic bombs.

science.q: Which of the following correctly describes the function of the nucleolus?
science.e: The nucleolus is primarily responsible for the synthesis and assembly of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and ribosome subunits.

science.q: The enrichment of water bodies with nutrients leading to algal blooms is called:
science.e: Eutrophication is the process where excess nutrients (nitrates, phosphates) cause rapid algal growth, depleting oxygen in water.

science.q: AIDS is caused by:
science.e: AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) is caused by HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus). HIV attacks CD4⁺ T cells (helper T cells), weakening the immune system. Transmitted through blood, sexual contact, or mother to child.

science.q: Two bodies of masses m and 2m are dropped from heights h and 2h respectively. Neglecting air resistance, the ratio of times taken to reach the ground is:
science.e: Time of free fall t ∝ √h, so ratio t1:t2 = √h : √(2h) = 1:√2.

science.q: Which of the following pairs represents the correct SI units of velocity and acceleration?
science.e: SI unit of velocity is m/s and of acceleration is m/s².

science.q: An exothermic reaction is one that:
science.e: Exothermic reactions release heat (negative enthalpy change, ΔH < 0). Examples: combustion of fuels, respiration, neutralization (acid + base), rusting of iron, formation of water. The surroundings feel warmer.

science.q: In the human reproductive system, the primary male sex hormone produced by the testes is:
science.e: Testosterone is responsible for development of male secondary sexual characteristics and sperm production.

science.q: In the context of climate change mitigation, which of the following carbon capture technologies directly removes CO2 from the ambient air rather than from point sources?
o: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage (BECCS)
science.e: Direct Air Capture (DAC) extracts CO2 from atmospheric air, while CCS captures from industrial point sources like power plants.

science.q: The process of converting a solid directly into a gas without passing through the liquid state is called sublimation. Which of the following substances undergoes sublimation at room temperature?
science.e: Iodine sublimes directly from solid to purple vapor at room temperature; others do not sublime.

science.q: The chemical name of 'washing soda' is:
science.e: Washing soda is hydrated sodium carbonate (Na2CO3·10H2O). Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3).

science.q: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with:
o: Same atomic number but different mass numbers (different neutrons)
Same mass number but different atomic number
Same protons and neutrons but different electrons
science.e: Isotopes have the same number of protons (same element) but different numbers of neutrons, hence different mass numbers. Example: Carbon-12, Carbon-13, Carbon-14 all have 6 protons but 6, 7, 8 neutrons respectively.

science.q: The process by which a cell engulfs large particles or microorganisms is called:
science.e: Phagocytosis is the engulfment of large solid particles by the cell membrane, forming a phagosome.

science.q: The full form of LASER is:
o: Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation
Light Amplified by Solar Energy Radiation
science.e: LASER = Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. Principle: stimulated emission — an excited atom emits a photon identical to the incident photon when struck by another photon. This creates a coherent, monochromatic, collimated beam. Applications: barcode scanners, CD/DVD players, su

science.q: The basic unit of life is the:
science.e: The cell is the basic structural, functional, and biological unit of all living organisms.

science.q: Which of the following hormones is secreted by the anterior pituitary gland and directly stimulates the production of thyroxine from the thyroid gland?
science.e: TSH is directly secreted by anterior pituitary to stimulate thyroid; TRH is from hypothalamus controlling TSH release; T3 is thyroid hormone; PTH is from parathyroid.

science.q: In a chemical reaction, the law of conservation of mass states:
o: Total mass of reactants = Total mass of products (Lavoisier, 1774)
Mass is not conserved in reactions
science.e: Antoine Lavoisier (1774) established: mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products. This is why chemical equations must be balanced.

science.q: In uniform circular motion, which of the following remains constant?
science.e: Speed is constant, so kinetic energy (½mv²) is constant; velocity and acceleration direction change, displacement varies.

science.q: Rusting of iron is a chemical process called:
science.e: Rusting is the corrosion of iron. It is an oxidation reaction: 4Fe + 3O2 + 6H2O → 4Fe(OH)3 (hydrated iron oxide). Moisture and oxygen are needed.

science.q: Which of the following is a primary pollutant?
science.e: Carbon monoxide is emitted directly from sources like vehicles, while the others are secondary pollutants formed in the atmosphere.

science.q: In a dicot stem, the arrangement of vascular bundles is best described as:
o: Concentric with xylem surrounded by phloem
science.e: Dicot stems typically have conjoint, collateral, open vascular bundles (cambium present) arranged in a ring.

science.q: The enzyme pepsin, which digests proteins in the stomach, is secreted in an inactive form called:
science.e: Pepsinogen is activated by hydrochloric acid to form active pepsin, preventing self-digestion of stomach lining.

science.q: The resistance of a conductor is inversely proportional to its?
science.e: Resistance R = ρL/A, so it is inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.

science.q: Which of the following is a primary pollutant that forms 'photochemical smog' in the presence of sunlight?
science.e: Nitrogen oxides (NOx) react with volatile organic compounds in sunlight to form photochemical smog.

tamil.e: புறநானூறு 400 பாடல்களைக் கொண்ட எட்டுத்தொகை நூல்களில் ஒன்றாகும்.

tamil.q: தமிழ் நெடுங்கணக்கில் உள்ள 'ங், ஞ், ண், ந், ம், ன்' ஆகிய மெய்யெழுத்துகள் எவ்வாறு அழைக்கப்படுகின்றன?
tamil.e: மெல்லின மெய்கள் (ங், ஞ், ண், ந், ம், ன்) மென்மையாக ஒலிப்பவை.

o: திருக்குறள், கம்பராமாயணம், பெரிய புராணம், சிலப்பதிகாரம், மணிமேகலை
tamil.e: ஐம்பெருங்காப்பியங்கள்: சிலப்பதிகாரம் (இளங்கோவடிகள்), மணிமேகலை (சீத்தலைச்சாத்தனார்), சீவகசிந்தாமணி (திருத்தக்கதேவர்), வளையாபதி, குண்டலகேசி.
தொல்காப்பியம் மெய்யெழுத்துக்கள் 18 என வரையறுக்கிறது.

tamil.q: திருநாவுக்கரசர் என்று அழைக்கப்படும் சைவ நாயன்மார் யார்?
tamil.e: அப்பர் திருநாவுக்கரசர் எனும் பெயரால் அறியப்படுகிறார்.
தேவாரம் ஞானசம்பந்தர், அப்பர், சுந்தரர் ஆகிய மூவரால் பாடப்பட்ட சைவத் திருமுறை நூலாகும்.
தேவாரம் சைவ நாயன்மார்களால் பாடப்பட்டது. திருஞானசம்பந்தர், திருநாவுக்கரசர் (அப்பர்), சுந்தரர் ஆகிய மூவர் பாடியவை சேர்க்கப்பட்டு திருமுறையாக வகைப்படுத்தப்பட்டது.

tamil.q: புலவர் குழந்தை யாரால் எழுதப்பட்ட 'இராவண காவியம்' எந்த கோணத்தில் ராமாயண கதையை கூறுகிறது?
tamil.e: புலவர் குழந்தை எழுதிய இராவண காவியம் இராவணனை நாயகனாக கொண்டு ராமாயண கதையை தமிழ் திராவிட மரபின் கோணத்தில் கூறுகிறது.

tamil.q: பக்தி இலக்கியத்தில் 'தேவாரம்' இயற்றிய மூவர்களில் ஒருவரல்லாதவர் யார்?
tamil.e: மாணிக்கவாசகர் தேவாரம் இயற்றிய மூவரில் அல்ல; அவர் திருவாசகம் இயற்றியவர்.

tamil.q: திருக்குறளின் மூன்று பால்களில் பொருள் பற்றிய பகுதி எது?
tamil.e: திருக்குறள் அறம், பொருள், இன்பம் என மூன்று பால்களில் பொருட்பால் பொருள் வளம் பற்றியது.
மணிமேகலை ஐம்பெருங்காப்பியங்களில் ஒன்று; இதன் ஆசிரியர் சாத்தனார்.
ஆழ்வார்கள் 12 பேர். இவர்கள் திருமால் பக்தர்கள். 63 நாயன்மார்கள் சைவத்தில் சிவ பக்தர்கள். ஆண்டாள் ஒரே பெண் ஆழ்வார். நம்மாழ்வார் திருவாய்மொழி பாடியவர்.
தொல்காப்பியம் எழுத்து, சொல், பொருள் என மூன்று அதிகாரங்களைக் கொண்டது. மூன்றாவது அதிகாரம் பொருளதிகாரம் ஆகும்.

tamil.q: ஐங்குறுநூறு நூலில் உள்ள பாடல்களின் எண்ணிக்கை எவ்வளவு?
tamil.e: ஐங்குறுநூறு ஐந்நூறு பாடல்களைக் கொண்ட புறப்பொருள் சார்ந்த சங்க இலக்கிய நூலாகும்.
சார்பெழுத்துகள் மொத்தம் 10 ஆகும் (உயிர்மெய், ஆய்தம், குற்றியலுகரம், முதலியன).

tamil.q: தொல்காப்பியத்தில் 'உயிர்மெய்' எழுத்துகள் பற்றிய விளக்கம் எவ்வாறு கூறப்படுகிறது?
tamil.e: உயிர்மெய் என்பது உயிரும் மெய்யும் சேர்ந்து பிறக்கும் எழுத்து வகையாகும். தொல்காப்பியம் இதனை எழுத்ததிகாரத்தில் விளக்குகிறது.
தொல்காப்பியம் புறத்திணைகளை ஏழாக வகைப்படுத்துகிறது.
ஆண்டாள் பன்னிரு ஆழ்வார்களில் ஒரே பெண் ஆழ்வார் ஆவார். இவர் பெரியாழ்வாரின் மகளாக வளர்ந்தவர்.
புறநானூறு புறப்பொருள் இலக்கியம். இது போர், வீரம், கொடை, அரசர் புகழ் பற்றிய 400 பாடல்களை கொண்டது.
திருக்குறளில் 'இல்வாழ்க்கை' எனும் அதிகாரம் (5ஆம் அதிகாரம், அறத்துப்பால் – இல்லறவியல்) இல்லற வாழ்க்கையின் சிறப்புகளை விளக்குகிறது.
வினைச்சொல் என்பது ஒரு செயலையோ நிலையையோ குறிக்கும் சொல்; அது காலம் காட்டும்.
திருக்குறளில் 133 அதிகாரங்கள் உள்ளன.
திருக்குறளின் அறத்துப்பால் 38 அதிகாரங்களைக் கொண்டது.
தொல்காப்பியம் மூன்று அதிகாரங்களைக் கொண்டது; எழுத்ததிகாரம் எழுத்துகளின் இலக்கணத்தை விளக்குகிறது.

tamil.q: திருக்குறளில் 'அன்பு' பற்றிய குறள் எந்த அதிகாரத்தில் இடம்பெற்றுள்ளது?
tamil.e: அன்புடைமை அதிகாரம் அறத்துப்பாலில் உள்ளது.

tamil.q: திருக்குறளின் முதல் குறள் எந்த அதிகாரத்தில் இடம்பெறுகிறது?
tamil.e: திருக்குறள் 'கடவுள் வாழ்த்து' அதிகாரத்துடன் தொடங்குகிறது.

tamil.q: பன்னிரு திருமுறைகளில் முதல் மூன்று திருமுறைகள் எவ்வாறு அழைக்கப்படுகின்றன?
tamil.e: முதல் மூன்று திருமுறைகளான சம்பந்தர், அப்பர், சுந்தரர் பாடல்கள் தேவாரம் எனப்படும்.
திருக்குறள் அறத்துப்பால், பொருட்பால், காமத்துப்பால் என மூன்று பால்களாக அமைந்துள்ளது.
இன்பத்துப்பால் 25 அதிகாரங்களைக் கொண்டது.
சிலப்பதிகாரத்தின் கதாநாயகி கண்ணகி ஆவார்.
சிலப்பதிகாரம் இளங்கோ அடிகளால் இயற்றப்பட்ட முதல் தமிழ்க் காப்பியமாகும்.

tamil.q: புணர்ச்சி விதிப்படி 'கல் + சிறு' என்பது எவ்வாறு புணரும்?
tamil.e: கல் என்பதன் இறுதி 'ல்' மெல்லினம், சிறு என்பதன் முதல் 'சி' வல்லினம்; புணர்ச்சியில் 'ல்' -> 'ற்' ஆகி 'கற்சிறு' ஆகும்.

tamil.q: திருக்குறளில் 'பொருள்' அதிகாரத்தின் கீழ் வரும் அதிகாரங்களின் எண்ணிக்கை எவ்வளவு?
tamil.e: திருக்குறளின் பொருட்பால் 70 அதிகாரங்களைக் கொண்டது (குறள் 381 முதல் 1080 வரை).

tamil.q: திருக்குறளில் 'நடுவு நிலை' பற்றி கூறும் அதிகாரத்தின் பெயர் என்ன?
tamil.e: நடுவு நிலைமை அதிகாரம் (12 ஆம் அதிகாரம்) நடுவுநிலை பற்றி கூறுகிறது.
திருக்குறளில் மொத்தம் 1330 குறட்பாக்கள் உள்ளன.

tamil.q: சிலப்பதிகாரத்தில் ஊர்க்காண் காதை எந்த ஊரை பற்றியது?
tamil.e: சிலப்பதிகாரம் மூன்று காண்டங்களை கொண்டது: புகார்க்காண்டம் (காவிரிப்பூம்பட்டினம்), மதுரைக்காண்டம் (மதுரை), வஞ்சிக்காண்டம் (வஞ்சி).
திருக்குறள் வெண்பா யாப்பில் அமைந்துள்ளது.

tamil.q: திருக்குறளில் 'அறன் வலியுறுத்தல்' அதிகாரத்தில் உள்ள குறள்களின் எண்ணிக்கை?
tamil.e: திருக்குறளின் ஒவ்வொரு அதிகாரமும் 10 குறள்களைக் கொண்டது.

tamil.q: சொல்லிலக்கணத்தில் 'தனிமொழி' மற்றும் 'தொடர்மொழி' குறித்து உரைக்கும் இயல் எது?
tamil.e: சொல்லிலக்கணம் தனிமொழி, தொடர்மொழி, புணர்ச்சி போன்றவற்றை விளக்குகிறது.
தொல்காப்பிய பொருளதிகாரம் மொத்தம் 9 இயல்களை கொண்டுள்ளது.

tamil.q: சங்க காலத்தில் புறப்பொருள் பாடல்களை மட்டும் கொண்ட நூல் எது?
tamil.e: புறநானூறு முழுவதும் புறப்பொருள் பாடல்களைக் கொண்ட எட்டுத்தொகை நூல்.

o: இரண்டு மாத்திரை அளவுள்ள எழுத்துக்கள் (ஆ, ஈ, ஊ, ஏ, ஐ, ஓ, ஔ)
tamil.e: நெட்டெழுத்துக்கள் என்பவை இரண்டு மாத்திரை அளவுள்ள நீண்ட உயிர் எழுத்துக்கள்: ஆ, ஈ, ஊ, ஏ, ஐ, ஓ, ஔ. இவை ஏழு ஆகும்.
உயிரும் மெய்யும் சேர்ந்து பிறக்கும் உயிர்மெய் எழுத்துகள் 216.
கைக்கிளை அகத்திணையின் ஒரு பகுதியாகும், இது ஒருதலைக் காதலைக் குறிக்கிறது.
திருஞானசம்பந்தர் 384 பதிகங்களைப் பாடியுள்ளார்.
ஆண்டாள் இயற்றிய திருப்பாவை வைணவப் பக்தி இலக்கியத்தின் முக்கிய நூல்.
சங்க காலத்தில் புலவர்களுக்கு கொடை வழங்கிய பெருந்தனக்காரர்கள் வள்ளல்கள் எனப்பட்டனர்.
காமத்துப்பால் (இன்பத்துப்பால்) 250 குறள்களைக் கொண்டது.
செய்யுளியல் பொருளதிகாரத்தின் ஒரு இயலாகும்.
'யாதனின் யாதனின் நீங்கியான்' என்பது 'துறவு' அதிகாரத்தின் முதல் குறள்.
பத்துப்பாட்டில் மிக நீளமான நூல் மதுரைக்காஞ்சி (782 அடிகள்); இயற்றியவர் மாங்குடி மருதனார்.

tamil.q: பழந்தமிழ் இலக்கண நூலான தொல்காப்பியம் மூன்று அதிகாரங்களைக் கொண்டது. அவை எவை?
tamil.e: தொல்காப்பியம் எழுத்து, சொல், பொருள் என மூன்று அதிகாரங்களைக் கொண்டது.
திருவாசகம் — மாணிக்கவாசகர் பாடிய சிவபக்திப் பாடல்கள். 'திருவாசகத்திற்கு உருகார் ஒரு வாசகத்திற்கும் உருகார்' என்ற பழமொழி புகழ் பெற்றது. எட்டாம் திருமுறை.
இடையின மெய் எழுத்துக்கள்: ய், ர், ல், வ், ழ், ள் — ஆறு எழுத்துக்கள். இவை வல்லினத்திற்கும் மெல்லினத்திற்கும் இடையே உள்ளன.
அகப்பொருளுக்குக் குறிஞ்சி, முல்லை, மருதம், நெய்தல், பாலை என ஐந்து திணைகள் உண்டு. மேலும் கைக்கிளை, பெருந்திணை என ஏழு திணைகளாகவும் கொள்ளலாம்.
மெய்ப்பாட்டியல் பொருளதிகாரத்தில் இடம்பெற்ற ஒரு இயல் ஆகும்.
